text.p: These are the leading stories in Serbian and Montenegrin press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- S E R B I A -
NASA BORBA
- Health workers' strike entering sixth week; Serbia central out-patiens' clinic will not receive patients while the emergency centre will receive only the most urgent cases.
- Serbian Transport and Communications Ministry gave Nis Television NTV six days to provide documents necessary for operating licence.
- Serbian electricity company hopes to get $100 million from the Serbian Development Fund for system overhauling.
- The Serbian Development Fund will grant three, six and nine-month loans for financing exports with a four to six percent annual interest rate.
- Serb-Serb dialogue on Kosovo is scheduled to be held in Belgrade on June 18.
POLITIKA

- Yugoslav Army Day, June 16, marks the same date in 1876 when the first military cooperation agreement was signed between Serbia and Montenegro, and is the confirmation of the firm and lasting alliance between the two peoples, said Yugoslav President Zoran Lilic.
- Relations between former Yugoslav republics will improve, says head of directorate of Yugoslav Left (JUL) Mira Markovic in an interview to Skopje daily.
- Yugoslav government proposed new customs tariffs regulations under which customs duty on luxury goods will be reduced by three percent.
- Over 120,000 Kosovo Albanians are to be returned home under the German-Yugoslav agreement signed in October 1996. So far over 200 have returned under the agreement.
BORBA
- The federal information law will be drafted in a few months, says Yugoslav Information Minister Goran Matic.
BLIC
- Sergeant shoots commander and then himself in the Kursumlija army barracks, in southern Serbia.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI

- In final text of draft law on ownership transformation, ten percent of a company's total capital to go into fund for frozen old hard currency savings, ten percent into pension fund, 60 percent free to workers and remaining 20 percent to be sold with or without a discount.

- Under new draft law on public holidays to be adopted by federal parliament at session on June 26, Yugoslav state holidays to include January 1 and 2 (New Year), April 27 (Statehood Day), May 9 (Victory Day), and November 29 and 30 (Day of transition from monarchy to a republican system).
- M O N T E N E G R O -
POBJEDA
- Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic opened the Yugoslav pavillion at the Venice Biennale.
- Montenegrin parliament resumed its session Monday to discuss the situation in state-owned media. The parliament agenda includes register of public officials' property and government reshuffle.

- The Yugoslav army arrested 400 Albanian smugglers illegally crossing the border in the last five months, commander of the Second Army General Bozidar Babic said. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
